item.title: Mutual transformations of arbitrary ternary qubit trees by Clifford gates
item.description: arXiv:2404.16693v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that ternary qubit trees with the same number of nodes can be transformed by the naturally defined sequence of Clifford gates into each other or into standard representation as one-dimensional chain corresponding to Jordan-Wigner transform.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Yu. Vlasov

item.title: Classification of Kirkwood-Dirac positivity-preserving unitaries
item.description: arXiv:2502.11784v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kirkwood-Dirac (KD) quasiprobability distributions are increasingly used across quantum information science, yet their computational significance remains unclear. We classify unitary dynamics that preserve KD positivity and connect this structure to classical simulation. In contrast to the discrete Wigner setting, we show that KD positivity preservation, stochastic evolution of quasiprobabilities, and preservation of total non-positivity do not coincide. We identify three classes of positivity-preserving unitaries: type I gates, which are exactly the KD-stochastic unitaries; type II gates, which are non-stochastic yet preserve total non-positivity by permuting and conjugating KD entries; and, for Fourier-conjugate bases in dimension $d=pq$, type III gates, which preserve KD positivity but can change the total non-positivity of non-real distributions. The classification is complete for Haar-random bases and for Fourier-conjugate dimensions $d=p^k$ and $d=pq$, with $p, q$ distinct primes. Adapting the sampling algorithm of Pashayan et al. [PRL 115, 070501], we simulate all of these positivity-preserving circuits efficiently on KD-positive inputs; type III gates, however, create a sharp distinction between real inputs, which remain efficiently simulable, and non-real inputs, whose sampling overhead can grow exponentially. Consequently, for $d=pq$ no resource theory can both treat the KD total non-positivity as a monotone and admit every efficiently simulable positivity-preserving unitary as a free operation.
item.dc:creator: J\k{e}drzej Burkat, Sergii Strelchuk

item.title: Macroscopic quantum coherence and entanglement in mechanical systems
item.description: arXiv:2503.08324v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The notion of a macroscopic quantum state must be pinned down in order to assess how well experiments probe the large-scale limits of quantum mechanics. However, the issue of quantifying so-called quantum macroscopicity is fraught with multiple approaches having varying interpretations and levels of computability and measurability. Here, we introduce two measures that capture independent macroscopic properties: i) extensive size, measuring the degree of coherence in position or momentum observables relative to atomic-scale units, and ii) entangled size, quantifying the number of entangled subsystems. These measures unify many desirable features of past proposals while having rigorously justified interpretations from quantum information theory in terms of coherence and multipartite entanglement. We demonstrate how to estimate them and obtain lower-bounds using experimental data from micro-mechanical oscillators and diffracting molecules. Notably, we find evidence for genuine multipartite entanglement of $10^5$ to $10^7$ atoms in recent mechanical superposition states.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Yadin, Matteo Fadel

item.title: Variational quantum-neural hybrid imaginary time evolution
item.description: arXiv:2503.22570v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Numerous methodologies have been proposed to implement imaginary-time evolution (ITE) on quantum computers. Among these, variational ITE (VITE) methods for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) computers have attracted much attention, as they use parameterized quantum circuits to mimic non-unitary dynamics. Although widely studied, conventional variational quantum algorithms face challenges in achieving high accuracy due to their strong dependence on the choice of ansatz quantum circuits. Recently, the variational quantum-neural hybrid eigensolver (VQNHE), which combines neural networks (NN) with a variational quantum eigensolver, has been proposed. This approach enhances the expressive power of variational states and improves the estimation of expectation values. Motivated by this idea, we explore the hybridization of VITE with an NN-based non-unitary operator. In this study, we propose a method named variational quantum-neural hybrid ITE (VQNHITE). By combining the NN with a parameterized quantum circuit, our proposal enhances the expressive power compared to conventional approaches, enabling more accurate tracking of imaginary-time dynamics. In addition, to mitigate the instability arising from randomly initialized NN parameters, we introduce an initial-parameter optimization procedure at a small imaginary-time step, which stabilizes the subsequent variational evolution. We tested our approach with numerical simulations on Heisenberg spin chains under both nearest-neighbor and all-to-all circuit connectivities. The results demonstrate that VQNHITE consistently achieves higher fidelity with the exact ITE state compared to VITE.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Kuji, Tetsuro Nikuni, Yuta Shingu

item.title: The Quantum Channels of the Compton Scattering of an Entangled Pair of Photons
item.description: arXiv:2504.04077v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Compton scattering of an entangled pair of photons is studied. Using the resulting reduced density matrix, we demonstrate how to derive the Kraus operators for the interaction from the underlying fundamental theory, quantum electrodynamics. The normalization of the final density matrix of the entangled photons after the interaction is crucial to obtaining the correct probabilities and correlations. The reduced density matrix of the photon, which does not participate in the interaction directly, remains unchanged. It indicates that quantum effects in quantum sensing using an entangled photon pair can be observed only through the correlations or superposition of the entire pair. We relate our results to the Stokes parameters for determining polarizations and investigating the entangled states of photons from electron-positron annihilation in astrophysical systems.
item.dc:creator: Chih-Yu Chen, C. D. Hu, Yeu Chung Lin

item.title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization Process for Data Imputation
item.description: arXiv:2505.04841v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data imputation is a critical preprocessing step, particularly in clinical datasets where missingness can bias downstream inference. We propose a quantum-inspired imputation framework and evaluate it on the UCI Pima Indians Diabetes dataset, where several physiological variables contain structural zeros that are treated as missing. The approach combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with quantum rotation-based reconstruction, where rotation angles are selected via gradient-free optimizers (Simulated Annealing, COBYLA, and Differential Evolution). For robustness, we retain the top three optimizer solutions per method and reconstruct missing values under distribution-aware bounds (e.g., $\pm 2$ standard deviations) and avoid unrealistic collapse toward central tendency. We also benchmark against (i) classical baselines (Mean, KNN, MICE, Decision Tree), (ii) modern matrix/ML imputers (SoftImpute, MissForest, VAE), and (iii) rotation/PCA controls (random orthogonal rotations and bootstrap PCA). Across the evaluated features, quantum-inspired variants achieve substantially improved distributional fidelity under Wasserstein W1 relative to modern baselines (e.g., the best quantum setting reduces average W1 by $\sim$66% vs. SoftImpute, $\sim$84% vs. MissForest, and $\sim$90% vs. VAE; and by $\sim$60% vs. Mean imputation), while remaining competitive with strong classical/control configurations. Dispersion is better preserved under the quantum-inspired methods, with variance/SD ratios closer to the observed data than (SoftImpute, MissForest, and VAE) and typically better than (Mean, KNN, MICE, and Decision Tree) on average. Overall, the results support quantum-inspired, optimization-guided rotations as a statistically grounded and scalable strategy for realistic imputation in healthcare and general AI pipelines, with a design that can be mapped to future quantum hardware as it matures.
item.dc:creator: Nishikanta Mohanty, Bikash K. Behera, Badshah Mukherjee, Pravat Dash, Christopher Ferrie

item.title: Entanglement Dimensionality of Continuous Variable States From Phase-Space Quasi-Probabilities
item.description: arXiv:2509.02743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dimensionality of entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number, is a core resource for quantum information processing. While its certification is well-established in finite-dimensional systems, many platforms harnessing high Schmidt numbers are natively continuous-variable (CV) systems, which are usually truncated to a finite subspace before canonical discrete-variable techniques are applied. For those instances, a core question is whether directly utilizing a genuinely CV toolbox leads to better and more robust characterisations. We answer this question by introducing Schmidt-number witnesses built directly from correlations and covariances of phase-space observables, accessible through characteristic- or Wigner-function measurements. They hold for arbitrary mixed states, including non-Gaussian ones, and only require correlations along a slice of phase space. We show that this direct estimation is more robust and versatile than first discretizing the system and using canonical discrete variable techniques. Moreover, we apply our method to certify arbitrarily-large Schmidt numbers of a bound-entangled Gaussian state. These results motivate genuine CV methods for characterizing high-dimensional entanglement across CV quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Shuheng Liu, Jiajie Guo, Matteo Fadel, Qiongyi He, Marcus Huber, Giuseppe Vitagliano

item.title: A parity obstruction to degree-optimal syndrome extraction in bivariate bicycle codes
item.description: arXiv:2509.26494v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Syndrome extraction for a CSS code has depth at least the Tanner-graph degree $\Delta$, attained by edge colouring if gate order is ignored; correctness adds a parity constraint. We prove three general obstructions to depth-$\Delta$ extraction and show that, for every two-block group-algebra code with weight-three polynomials whose checks overlap in at most two qubits, no correct single-round circuit with one ancilla per check and one CNOT per Tanner edge has depth six: the minimum is seven, so the seven-layer cycle of Bravyi \emph{et al.} is optimal for their seven bivariate bicycle codes. This is the first analytic, family-wide impossibility result, extending prior instance-specific solver-based infeasibility results. The hypothesis cannot be dropped: a single orbit of four-qubit overlaps with a collision element of even order and $2$-height at most eight makes depth six attainable, and a $[[72,8,6]]$ code of this kind has a verified six-layer circuit. The refutations carry DRAT certificates.
item.dc:creator: Guangyi Li, Yu Gan, Zeguan Wu, Xueyue Zhang, Zheshen Zhang, Junyu Liu

item.title: Optimal phase estimation in the presence of correlated dephasing
item.description: arXiv:2511.07211v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate optimal metrological protocols for phase estimation in the presence of correlated dephasing noise, including spin-squeezed state sensing strategies as well as parallel and adaptive protocols optimized using tensor-network-based numerical methods. The results are benchmarked against fundamental bounds obtained either via the latest quantum comb extension method or an optimized classical simulation method. We find that the spin-squeezed states offer practically optimal performance in the regime where phase fluctuations are positively correlated but can be outperformed by tensor-network-optimized strategies for negatively correlated fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Srijon Ghosh, Arkadiusz Kobus, Stanis{\l}aw Kurdzia{\l}ek, Rafa{\l} Demkowicz-Dobrza\'nski

item.title: Single-step phase-engineered pulse for active readout cavity reset with a known qubit state
item.description: arXiv:2512.08393v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a circuit QED architecture, we experimentally demonstrate a hardware-efficient and qubit-state-dependent Single-Step Phase-Engineered (SSPE) pulse scheme for actively depopulating a readout cavity. The protocol appends a reset segment with tailored amplitude and phase to a square readout pulse. Within the linear-response regime, the optimal reset amplitude scales proportionally with the readout amplitude, while the optimal reset phase remains invariant, significantly simplifying the experimental calibration procedure. For a known qubit state, time-resolved measurements demonstrate that the SSPE pulse achieves faster cavity depletion than the CLEAR protocol. Crucially, this approach enables arbitrarily fast, overshoot-free depletion of the cavity photon population, with the ultimate reset rate constrained by the available drive amplitude and the finite analog bandwidth of the measurement chain. A comprehensive evaluation of the QND character reveals no measurable increase in non-QNDness relative to the free-decay and CLEAR protocols. The remaining non-QNDness is predominantly attributable to state switching induced by qubit relaxation during the readout process. These results establish the SSPE scheme as a practical and scalable approach for achieving rapid and smooth cavity reset in superconducting quantum circuits in the case of a known qubit state.
item.dc:creator: Ren-Ze Zhao, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Peng Wang, Sheng Zhang, Xiao-Yan Yang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Sheng-Ri Liu, Peng Duan, Guo-Ping Guo

item.title: Universal Statistics of Measurement-Induced Entanglement in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
item.description: arXiv:2512.13809v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the statistics of measurement-induced entanglement (MIE) after partial measurement on a class of one-dimensional quantum critical states described by Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids at low energies. Using a replica trick to average over measurement outcomes in the charge basis and tools from conformal field theory (CFT), we derive closed-form expressions for the cumulants of MIE. We show that exact Born-averaging over microscopic measurement outcomes becomes equivalent at low energy to averaging over conformal boundary conditions weighted by their corresponding partition functions. Our results yield distinctive critical behavior across all cumulants in the regime where the unmeasured parts of the system are maximally separated. We also obtain the full distribution of MIE, finding that it is generically bimodal and exhibits fat-tails. We corroborate our analytical predictions by numerical calculations and find good agreement between them.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Khanna, Romain Vasseur

item.title: Evolutionary BP+OSD Decoding for Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
item.description: arXiv:2512.18273v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) for fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a balanced decoding solution that offers high performance, low complexity, and low latency. However, the de facto standard - belief propagation (BP) combined with ordered statistics decoding (OSD) - suffers from excessive iterations in the BP stage and high complexity in the OSD stage. To address these challenges, we propose an evolutionary BP (EBP) decoder optimized via a differential evolution (DE) algorithm. By leveraging the gradient-free nature of DE, we enable end-to-end optimization of the EBP+OSD structure to maximize overall performance. In addition, a multi-objective selection rule is introduced to suppress frequent OSD activation, significantly reducing complexity overhead. Simulation results on surface codes and quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes demonstrate that EBP+OSD simultaneously achieves both superior decoding performance and substantially lower complexity compared to conventional BP+OSD, particularly in stringent low-latency regimes.
item.dc:creator: Hee-Youl Kwak, Seong-Joon Park, Hyunwoo Jung, Jeongseok Ha, Jae-Won Kim

item.title: Learning Hamiltonians for $O(1)$ Oracle-Query Quantum State Preparation
item.description: arXiv:2512.19181v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a Hamiltonian-based quantum state preparation method implemented via a shallow parametrized quantum circuit. The approach learns the parameters of a diagonal Hamiltonian through a classical training phase, while the quantum circuit itself performs only fixed-depth Hamiltonian evolution and mixing operations. With oracle access to the learned Hamiltonian parameters, $N$ classical data values can be encoded into $n=\log_2{N}$ qubits using $O(1)$ quantum queries, shifting the overall computational cost to an $O(N\log{N})$ classical preprocessing stage. For structured datasets generated by an underlying function, oracle access can be avoided by expressing the Hamiltonian in the Walsh basis and retaining only a polynomial number of significant terms. In this regime, quantum state preparation is achieved in $\text{poly}(n)$ time using $\text{poly}(n)$ parameters, reaching infidelities on the order of $10^{-5}$. By restricting the Hamiltonian to one-local and two-local terms, the method naturally yields hardware-efficient circuits suitable for near-term quantum devices. This separation keeps the quantum execution shallow while moving optimization to classical computation.
item.dc:creator: Sadegh Salami, Mohammad T. Manzuri, Mehdi Ramezani, Sina Asadiyan Zargar, Abolfazl Bahrampour, Alireza Bahrampour

item.title: High Fidelity Single-NV Qubit Quantum State Tomography by Photoelectric Readout
item.description: arXiv:2603.16502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond is one of the advanced candidates for solid-state quantum computing at room temperature and has proven to be competitive in terms of gate fidelity and the availability of quantum error correction codes. Ambient solid-state qubits may therefore provide quantum computing architectures as an alternative to current solutions. The NV center has an associated electronic spin that is conventionally read out via photoluminescence. As an alternative, the electrical readout is not limited by the confocal resolution of quantum microscopes, which is required in the development of NV-based quantum processors to establish a scalable individual single-spin readout on the order of a few nanometers (necessary for strong dipole-dipole coupling). In this work, the performance of photoelectric readout versus traditional optical readout is investigated to perform Quantum State Tomography measurements on a single NV center. A state fidelity of 0.995 $\pm$ 0.006 is achieved using photoelectrical spin-state readout for state reconstruction, comparable to simultaneous optical measurements. We report photocurrent signal delays, which significantly slow down the photocurrent tomography. We develop a model describing their origin, and propose strategies for their mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Boo Carmans, Michael Petrov, Milos Nesladek

item.title: Depth dependence of entanglement and circuit complexity in random linear optical networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.14277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the growth of entanglement and circuit complexity in random passive linear optical networks as a function of the circuit depth. For entanglement dynamics, we start with an initial Gaussian state with all $n$ modes equally squeezed. For random brickwork circuits, we show that entanglement, as measured by the R\'enyi-2 entropy, grows diffusively as a function of the depth, in contrast to the linear growth for random qubit brickwork circuits. In the other direction, for arbitrary circuit geometries we prove bounds on depths which ensure the average-case subsystem entanglement reaches within a constant factor of the maximum value in all subsystems, and bounds which ensure closeness of the random linear optical unitary to a Haar random unitary in $L^2$ Wasserstein distance. We also consider robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits, as measured by the minimum number of gates required in any circuit that approximately implements the linear optical unitary. Viewing this as a function of the number of modes and the circuit depth, we show the robust circuit complexity for random one-dimensional brickwall circuits scales at most diffusively in the depth with high probability, again in contrast to the linear scaling for certain random qubit circuits. The corresponding Gaussian unitary $\tilde{\mathcal U}$ for the approximate implementation retains high output fidelity $|\langle\psi|\mathcal U^\dagger \tilde{\mathcal U}|\psi\rangle|^2$ for pure states $|\psi\rangle$ with constrained expected photon-number.
item.dc:creator: Laura Shou, Joseph T. Iosue, Yu-Xin Wang, Victor Galitski, Alexey V. Gorshkov

item.title: Spin Kerr-cat qubits
item.description: arXiv:2604.19687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The use of noise-robust qubit encodings provides a way of extending the lifetime of quantum information at the hardware level. In this work, we introduce the spin Kerr-cat encoding, which leverages a sweet spot near a clock transition in the spectrum of quadrupolar nuclei (having spin $I\geq 1$) to achieve a suppression of charge and magnetic noise leading to qubit dephasing. The basis states of the spin Kerr-cat qubit are given by the two lowest levels of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric nuclear-spin Hamiltonian and are well approximated by spin cat states for sufficiently high asymmetry parameters. For nuclei in highly asymmetric electric-field gradients, the nuclear spin could therefore be initialized in the spin-Kerr-cat subspace using SU(2) rotations and measurement rather than full SU($2I+1$) control. We calculate the dephasing time of the spin Kerr-cat qubit under a model of $1/f$ noise, as well as relaxation of the qubit due to breaking of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry by charge-noise-induced fluctuations of the quadrupolar tensor. Using measured parameters for antimony (${}^{123}\mathrm{Sb}$) donors in silicon, we estimate that second-scale $T_2^*$ times could be achieved with this encoding, with bitflips and leakage occurring on significantly longer timescales. We propose a two-qubit gate acting on spin Kerr-cat qubits and electron-spin qubits, enabled by adiabatically moving an electron on and off the donor potential. Based on numerical simulations, we estimate that with an enhancement of measured quadrupolar couplings by a factor of ${\approx} 2$, a gate fidelity exceeding $99\%$ could be achieved for spin Kerr cats encoded in ${}^{123}\mathrm{Sb}$, with a gate time under $100$ ns. By entangling the nuclear spin with an electron spin in this way, the spin Kerr-cat qubit could then be measured using a Pauli spin blockade readout of the electron.
item.dc:creator: Z. M. McIntyre, Daniel Loss

item.title: Experimental subdiffraction source discrimination enabled by spatial demultiplexing and single-photon detectors
item.description: arXiv:2605.15929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a universal, parameter-independent test for asymmetric source discrimination below the diffraction limit. The test exploits spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) and single-photon detection to discriminate the presence of a faint source in the vicinity of a brighter one. We develop a complete theory of the test in the presence of arbitrary modal crosstalk and show that the crosstalk-affected test retains a favorable error exponent over diffraction-limited direct imaging, provided that the crosstalk remains below a threshold $C_{\mathrm{max}}\simeq 1/9$. This establishes a quantitative condition under which the subdiffraction advantage of SPADE survives realistic imperfections. We experimentally test the scheme for a range of source separations and intensity ratios, without requiring prior knowledge of these parameters. The measured false-negative error rates are in good agreement with the theoretical model and systematically outperform direct imaging. These results demonstrate that SPADE provides a robust and experimentally accessible advantage for asymmetric subdiffraction hypothesis testing in the photon-starved regime, even in the presence of realistic modal crosstalk.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Santamaria Amato, Danilo Triggiani, Cosmo Lupo

item.title: Measurement of quantum states and nonlocal correlations
item.description: arXiv:2605.21243v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the major remaining questions concerning foundations of the quantum mechanical theory is how superpositions are measured such that definite outcomes are obtained. Here a resolution to that issue is proposed. It is shown how to obtain state vectors associated with measurements on the separated subystems of an entangled state, revealing how a single wavefunction encodes a special kind of set of statistical measurement outcomes. The result explains why measurements on the subsystems give definite outcomes and why measurements on one subsystem are correlated with those on the other. It is therefore concluded that the theory of quantum mechanics, without nonlinearities or \emph{ad hoc} assertions, can explain both the mechanism of state vector collapse and the reason for the paradoxical nonlocal correlations between separated subsystems. The theory also explains why nonlocal correlations do not require any kind of interaction between the subsystems.
item.dc:creator: Grgeory D. Scholes

item.title: Demonstration of tripartite cat states in two distinct classes of entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2607.12317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics and an essential resource for quantum computation, communication, and metrology. While bipartite entanglement is extensively studied, genuine multipartite entangled states remain largely inaccessible in the continuous-variable domain. Here, we experimentally realize continuous-variable tripartite entangled cat states of the two distinct classes with fundamentally inequivalent properties, namely GHZ-cat and W-cat states, encoded across three microwave resonators coupled to an ancillary superconducting transmon. We develop one-to-all conditional controls on the three oscillators by fully utilizing three energy levels of the transmon to generate these states in a single piece of hardware and employ an efficient subspace tomography protocol for state reconstruction. We obtain measurement-corrected state fidelities of $0.83\pm0.02$ for GHZ-cat and $0.70\pm0.02$ for W-cat, both exceeding the thresholds for genuine multipartite entanglement, with the W-state certification further supported by an optimized fully decomposable witness directly computed with the reconstructed density matrix. We validate the distinct entanglement classes by experimentally demonstrating that pairwise entanglement is present in the W-cat state but absent in the GHZ-cat state. Our technique for the on-demand generation and characterization of inequivalent classes of tripartite continuous-variable entanglement provides a testbed for studying multipartite bosonic entanglement and its robustness to loss, and a building block for future quantum information processing with multipartite bosonic codes.
item.dc:creator: May Chee Loke, Jonathan Schwinger, Kehui Yu, Yingshan Zhang, Amon M. Kasper, Tanjung Krisnanda, Yvonne Y. Gao

item.title: Highly integrated quantum key distribution transmitter enabled by silicon photonics
item.description: arXiv:2607.23413v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides information-theoretic security independent of computational assumptions, yet the bulk and cost of current systems hinder large-scale deployment. Although integrated photonic technologies have enabled highly integrated QKD chips, practical QKD transmitters are still predominantly implemented as rack-mounted systems. Here, we demonstrate a highly integrated standalone QKD transmitter that integrates all essential functionalities required for practical QKD operation within a compact platform built around a silicon photonic encoding chip. The transmitter occupies only $167 \times 56 \times 21~\mathrm{mm}^3$ ($\sim 0.2~\mathrm{dm}^3$), comparable in size to a half-height, half-width PCIe card and more than 30 times smaller in volume than a conventional 1U rack-mounted system. Paired with a conventional discrete-component receiver, it achieves a secure key rate of 219.1 kbps over 51.3 km of standard single-mode fiber, with performance comparable to that of conventional discrete-component implementations. This work bridges the gap between photonic chip integration and deployable QKD hardware, marking an important step toward transitioning QKD transmitters from conventional rack-mounted equipment to compact board-level platforms.
item.dc:creator: Rende Liu, Yan-Lin Tang, Cheng-Guang Dong, Yan Ma, Guo-Qing Liu, Zhi-Lin Xie, Shuai Li, Mi Zou, Hao Liang, Shi-biao Tang

item.title: Microscopic study of topological phase transitions: Percolation point of view
item.description: arXiv:2607.26707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate microscopic mechanisms underlying decoherence-induced transitions between topologically ordered states. As a first case study, we analyze the color code using topological entanglement negativity (TEN) and a disorder parameter associated with 1-form symmetry. We interpret these quantities as first- and zeroth-dimensional simplicial homological objects, respectively, and show that the transition can be understood in terms of decoherence percolation. To resolve its local structure, we introduce quasi-local TEN (QLTEN), which visualizes the spatial distribution of local topological properties and the growth of decohered regions. We further introduce explosive percolation (EP), corresponding here to biased decoherence that suppresses the formation of large decohered clusters. As a second case study, we consider the toric code on a triangular lattice under external-field-type decoherence. Numerical results show that QLTEN faithfully captures the emergence of Higgs regions and the survival of logical qubits. Although global TEN, QLTEN clusters, and string operators are strongly correlated in both models, the color code and toric code respond differently to EP patterns. This difference indicates that a universal microscopic description of decoherence-induced topological phase transitions remains challenging even for closely related systems.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Kataoka, Ikuo Ichinose

item.title: Exact minimum measurement dependence for faithful local deterministic models of multipartite GHZ-Mermin correlations
item.description: arXiv:2608.00124v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A local deterministic model can reproduce Bell-inequality violations only if the hidden state depends on the measurement settings. Hall found the minimum such dependence for the singlet state [Phys. Rev. Lett. 105, 250404 (2010)] and posed the corresponding problem for the Mermin state [Phys. Rev. A 84, 022102 (2011)]. This paper solves it, for the $n$-party GHZ-Mermin scenario at every $n \geq 3$, with the marginals reproduced as well as the correlators. The minimum measurement-dependence fraction is $F_{\min}(n) = R/[2(R+1)]$, with $R = 2^{\lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor}$ the Mermin violation ratio: $1/3, 2/5, 4/9, 8/17, \ldots$, always below $1/2$. The lower bound follows from Mermin's inequality by a general overlap bound; the upper bound is an explicit model, uniform on the hidden-variable classes that violate the fewest constraints, with closed-form counts; a reduction theorem shows that for Mermin scenarios the marginals impose no additional dependence. The Mermin values are also certified by integer-arithmetic enumeration through $n = 22$. The formula was stated as a conjecture in the first version of this paper and was first proved, by a different route, by Wang, Yao and Chen; the proof here was obtained independently and the two agree. Every minimal contradiction of size $k$ among stabilizer constraints has correlator-only minimum $1/(k-1)$. With the marginals included the minimum is the same on every core of the $C_5$ ring cluster, on the size-4 and size-5 cores of $C_4$ and on every four-core of $C_6$, but larger on the size-6 and size-7 cores of $C_4$ and on 112 of the 1,920 five-cores of $C_6$, with exact certificates on both sides in every case.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Alai

item.title: Exact quantum circuits for a lattice Boltzmann realization of the Dirac equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.06570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quantum lattice Boltzmann scheme of Succi and Dellar advances a four-component Dirac spinor on a lattice by a fixed sequence of local, exactly norm-preserving operations: a basis rotation, a collision, a streaming shift, and the inverse rotation. While this correspondence has been noted qualitatively, it has remained unclear whether it can be realized exactly and unitarily as a gate-model quantum circuit. This unitarity is a structural property of the scheme, which should, in principle, enable an operator-by-operator port onto quantum hardware. We give a gate-level construction of every operation of the three-dimensional Dirac QLB scheme: the fixed rotation gates, the collision gate, the streaming shift as a controlled increment on a position register, the position-dependent potential as a phase oracle, and periodic and reflecting boundary conditions as unitary circuits. Together, these constructions provide the first complete demonstration that the scheme is exactly representable in the gate model without any approximation beyond the classical method itself. We then compose them into single-axis, two- and three-dimensional time steps. On a state-vector emulator the resulting circuits reproduce the classical QLB solver to machine precision, thus verifying our quantum implementation. Our aim is representability and correctness rather than computational speedup; questions of state preparation, asymptotic cost, and hardware noise are identified as open avenues for future work. Appendices restore physical units, derive the scheme's Zitterbewegung in closed form and compare it with a trapped-ion simulation, and execute a reduced two-site instance on a Rigetti superconducting processor, where choosing the qubits from the live calibration lowers the state-preparation error. All operators, circuits, and figures are reproducible from the open-source quantumKineticMethods library.
item.dc:creator: Nilesh Sawant, Ethan Young, Kevin Patrick Griffin, Michael Martin

item.title: Constructing and characterising anharmonic potentials in a harmonic oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2609.02405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum systems offer a natural platform for quantum information processing and analogue quantum simulation of real-world processes. Realising these applications, however, requires anharmonic potentials with programmable functional forms, which are challenging to engineer on demand. Here, in a superconducting harmonic oscillator coupled to a transmon qubit, we construct programmable non-Gaussian phase gates $e^{-iV(\hat{X})}$, corresponding to the impulsive action of an anharmonic potential $V(\hat{X})$, and characterise them by reconstructing their corresponding force pointwise. Using bosonic quantum signal processing, we compile target potentials into modular circuits of qubit rotations interleaved with a fixed conditional-displacement primitive. We first demonstrate a cubic phase gate whose cubic nature is jointly validated by the resulting non-Gaussian states and the force reconstructed pointwise from the gate's action on coherent probe states. We then construct a family of double-well potentials and use the reconstructed force to witness the double-well topology and tunable asymmetry. Finally, we engineer an approximate Morse potential and obtain its force profile using position-compressed probes, which extend reliable reconstruction towards the steep repulsive wall. These results establish a programmable route to constructing the potential landscape of quantum harmonic oscillators and a practical method for reconstructing its spatial structure, providing a building block for quantum simulation of anharmonic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Clara Yun Fontaine, Mansi Somani, Kehui Yu, May Chee Loke, Jonathan Schwinger, Pak-Tik Fong, Ni-Ni Huang, Adrian Copetudo, Mustafa Bakr, Hoi-Kwan Lau, Tanjung Krisnanda, Yvonne Y. Gao

item.title: Energetic Costs of Subspace Quantum Error Correction
item.description: arXiv:2609.03825v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum error correction acts as an entropy pump, transferring noise-induced uncertainty from a protected quantum system into syndrome information stored in an auxiliary memory. Repeated operation requires this memory to be cleared which unavoidably contributes to the energetic cost of error correction. Here, we characterise this contribution for subspace quantum error-correcting codes and identify how it depends on the joint structure of the code, the noise, and the representation of the retained syndrome information. Starting from the Knill--Laflamme conditions, we construct an effective syndrome state whose von Neumann entropy sets a lower bound on the ideal work required to maintain a reusable syndrome register. Projective syndrome readout generally generates additional entropy, and we quantify the resulting gap through measurement inefficiency. We then specialise to stabiliser codes under independent local Pauli noise and analyse two classical levels of syndrome representation. At the level of abstract error labels, degeneracies among single-qubit errors reduce the leading-order entropy of processed recovery labels. At the parity-check level, lower-weight checks reduce the marginal entropy generated by individual measurement outcomes in the low-noise regime. We identify the additional burden associated with retaining and separately erasing these outcomes as a bit-level inefficiency, and illustrate both costs for the five-qubit, Steane, generalised Shor, and rotated surface codes. Our results establish a hierarchy of syndrome-memory energetic costs and identify the code, noise, and measurement structures that control the ideal thermodynamic burden of subspace quantum error correction.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Czartowski, Felix C. Binder

item.title: Transition between weak and strong measurements in the presence of post-selection
item.description: arXiv:2609.04812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the weak measurement regime, post-selection can result in the observation of anomalous weak values, seemingly contradicting the eigenvalue statistics observed when the measurement interaction is strong. Here, we investigate the dependence of meter statistics on measurement strength in a post-selected measurement. We find that the meter statistics in the intermediate regime between weak and strong measurements is nearly independent of measurement strength and show that, in this regime, the system performs a measurement of momentum on the meter. Our results show that post-selection is extremely sensitive to the action of the meter on the system, highlighting the difference between the weak measurement regime where this back-action is negligible and the average meter position is a valid measurement result, and the intermediate regime where the meter statistics should not be misinterpreted as a measurement outcome. The transition between weak values and eigenvalues is facilitated by a reversal of the roles of the system and the meter, where the post-selection acts as a readout of information about the meter. The intermediate measurement regime thus reveals that the apparent contradictions between anomalous weak values and eigenvalues originate from the non-classical effects of back-action on the post-selected meter statistics.
item.dc:creator: Shogo Hanashiro, Holger F. Hofmann

item.title: Generalized Fidelity, the Data Processing Inequality, and Convexity
item.description: arXiv:2609.09753v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show that the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance induced by the generalized fidelity fails the data processing inequality (DPI) in every dimension $n\geq2$. In dimension two, we derive three sufficient conditions guaranteeing the DPI by using an explicit formula for the real part of the generalized fidelity. Furthermore, we find a necessary and sufficient condition under which the generalized fidelity reduces to the Uhlmann fidelity. We also show that neither the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance nor its square is convex in one state, even with the other state and the reference fixed, in every dimension $n\geq2$.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Reza Rajaei, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Fast Evaluation of the Sixth-Order Time-Convolutionless (TCL6) Master-Equation Generator
item.description: arXiv:2609.18806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Higher-order time-convolutionless (TCL) master equations provide systematic corrections for non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, but their time-ordered integrals become increasingly costly to evaluate. Direct quadrature of the Hadamard-reduced sixth-order (TCL6) generator at all $N_t$ sampled times requires $O(N_t^3)$ operations at fixed system dimension. We derive an exact reduction for a finite-dimensional system coupled through one Hermitian operator to a stationary centered Gaussian bath. By separating operator coefficients from scalar time-dependent spectral densities, the complete TCL6 time series is reduced to cumulative sums and first-order recurrences, one-dimensional causal convolutions, and an exact dyadic recursion for interlocked sums. With the algorithm, evaluating the complete TCL6 time series requires $O(N_t\log^2N_t)$ operations. These reductions enable fast, practical simulations of non-Markovian dynamics involving multiphonon and multiphoton processes in open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Chen, Sirui Chen, Dragomir Davidovic

item.title: Long-horizon autoformalization of a core theorem underlying MIP* = RE
item.description: arXiv:2609.19814v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Landmark mathematical formalizations have taken specialist teams years to complete. We present FormalFlow, a system that coordinates AI proving agents under human supervision to address statement drift and proof composition in long-horizon formalization. Drawing on software-engineering principles and practices, it uses a shared blueprint to guide nested planning, proving, and review loops. Using FormalFlow, we completed a machine-checked Lean 4 proof of the quantum soundness of the classical low individual-degree test, a core theorem underlying MIP* = RE, in 63 days. The final library contains 126,367 lines of Lean code, all generated by agents. Beyond providing a verified foundation for quantum complexity, the formalization corrects side conditions and intermediate error bounds in the published proof and improves the error exponent of the main theorem. The development record shows what it takes to trust proofs written by AI agents and provides reusable tools for verifying research mathematics at scale.
item.dc:creator: Sirui Lu, Ruixuan Deng, Yanqiao Zhu, Zhengfeng Ji

item.title: Discrete semiclassical theory of quantum-thermal escape
item.description: arXiv:2609.21625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dissipationless quantum-thermal escape rate from a metastable well is often written as a Boltzmann average of the Hill-Wheeler flux over a continuum of energies. This continuum treatment diverges exponentially at low temperature, because it pairs the quantum partition function of the well with a classical flux integral. Retaining the discrete nature of the quasibound spectrum removes the divergence exactly, and the resulting rate is obtained in closed form on both sides of the crossover temperature $T_0$. Evaluating a uniform Kemble transmission probability on Bohr-Sommerfeld levels further removes the parabolic-barrier error and recovers the WKB decay rate of the lowest resonance at zero temperature. Benchmarked against the resonances of cubic and quintic potentials, obtained by complex scaling, this uniform semiclassical rate stays within $9\%$ of the exact one over eleven orders of magnitude. Below $T_0$, the rate rises above its zero-temperature plateau with the level spacing as activation energy, and the plateau ends at a temperature $T_1$ noticeably below $T_0$. In an isolated well, whose levels are not replenished, the thermal rate is only the initial slope of a decay which ceases to be single exponential at $T_1$, while at $T_0$ the initial escape moves from tunneling inside the well to the barrier top. We discuss implications for Josephson junctions, single-electron pumps, and nuclear burning in dense stellar matter.
item.dc:creator: Luca Salasnich, Cesare Vianello

item.title: Observation of Universal Quantum Chaos at Shallow Depths
item.description: arXiv:2609.28623v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universal statistical laws are a hallmark of quantum chaos. A natural route to probing them in quantum circuits is offered by the statistics of output probabilities, which for sufficiently deep chaotic circuits approach the Porter--Thomas distribution. Here we show, theoretically and experimentally, that the approach to this limit is itself universal, and is organized into geometry-dependent universality classes. At shallow depths, growing only logarithmically with system size, we derive universal output-probability distributions that differ markedly from Porter--Thomas statistics, and we test them on a programmable superconducting processor. Two-dimensional lattices, open one-dimensional chains, and periodic rings exhibit distinct universal forms, retaining signatures of geometry and boundary topology within the same logarithmic-depth regime. Within each class, the distributions depend on only two parameters: an effective many-body Thouless scale and the accumulated number of incoherent errors. Extracting these directly from measured bitstring frequencies provides access to scrambling, entanglement growth of the target state, and global fidelity, without reconstructing or classically simulating the implemented circuit. We also identify a noise-driven transition between output statistics retaining system-wide quantum correlations and those reproducible by independent small patches. Our results establish universality beyond Porter--Thomas statistics as a quantitative tool for characterizing noisy quantum processors.
item.dc:creator: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Hugo L\'oio, Thomas J. Maldonado, Shashwat Kumar, Pedram Roushan, Andrea De Luca, Jacopo De Nardis

item.title: Spectral Analysis Beyond the Spectral Gap: Rapid Mixing of Quantum Gibbs Samplers in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.05848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove rapid mixing of a quantum Gibbs sampler for general one-dimensional non-commuting local spin systems at every fixed positive temperature. In particular, for a system of $n$ sites, we show that the Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed-balanced Gibbs sampler of~\cite{CKG2023} converges from any initial state to trace-norm error $\epsilon$ in time $O(\log^4(n)+\log(1/\epsilon))$. This improves the previous $O(n+\log(1/\epsilon))$ bound and establishes rapid mixing beyond high-temperature and weak-interaction regimes. Our proof explains why the slowest decay rate, captured by the spectral gap, can substantially underestimate the speed of equilibration. The key insight is that a state far from equilibrium must have a substantial component outside the span of low-weight Pauli operators, where stronger dissipation estimates apply. This yields two stages of relaxation: a double-exponential convergence from a bad initial state, followed by exponential convergence near equilibrium. We turn this mechanism into a framework for proving rapid mixing through spectral analysis beyond the gap. Our decay estimate is equivalent to exponential convergence in sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. Together with the spectral gap, it also implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality with rate $\Omega(\log^{-4}(n))$.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding

item.title: Decoupling ultrastrong Rabi splitting from quantum vacuum dressing in a chiral cavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.10944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Polariton formation and quantum vacuum dressing are usually regarded as intertwined consequences of ultrastrong light--matter coupling. Here we show that they can be selectively controlled through the relative direction of rotation of the cavity field and the matter excitation. We consider cyclotron resonance coupled to a chiral cavity supporting a single circularly polarized mode. We quantize the electromagnetic field within the cavity, derive from first principles the Hamiltonian, and investigate how mode hybridization and vacuum dressing are rendered as we tune the magnetic field. When the cavity field co-rotates with the cyclotron motion, energy is exchanged resonantly between light and matter, producing a large Rabi splitting and conventional polaritons, while the ground state remains the bare vacuum. Reversing the magnetic field makes the cyclotron motion counter-rotating with the cavity field. The same cavity mode then couples through anomalous processes that create and annihilate light and matter excitations in pairs: the conventional polaritonic anticrossing disappears, while the ground state acquires squeezing and virtual excitations. Our results show that spectral hybridization and quantum vacuum dressing are distinct manifestations of ultrastrong coupling, offering an additional degree of freedom for engineering cavity quantum materials.
item.dc:creator: Ayoub El-Amrani, Nasir Boubekraoui, Zakaria Mzaouali, Houssam Sabri, Herschel Rabitz, Abdelouahed El Fatimy, Dukhyung Lee

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the second of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on Shelah's independence property. An observable without it has idealized responses of the first Baire class, and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy for Rosenthal compacta divides such observables into three classes, each containing a physical order. In the transverse-field Ising model, the spontaneous magnetization decides whether the family of magnetizations is stable or lies in the second class.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Continuity of certain quantum channel divergences
item.description: arXiv:2610.16270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The geometric channel fidelity, the geometric R\'enyi divergences and the Belavkin--Staszewski relative entropy give converse bounds for capacities, discrimination and estimation. Channels are known only approximately, yet two pairs of channels with equal sums can be arbitrarily close in the diamond norm and have fidelities $0$ and $1$. The remedy is the Arveson--Radon--Nikodym derivative $T$ of one map with respect to the sum $\Omega$, whose transpose is the environment effect selecting that map in a Stinespring dilation of $\Omega$. In $T$, these quantities and all maximal $f$-divergences of operator convex $f$ are continuous, with explicit dimension-free moduli; for two pairs of channels with the same sum the fidelities differ by at most $2\|T_1-T_2\|_\infty^{1/2}$, which gives H\"older continuity in the diamond norm on such splittings. The fidelity is continuous at a pair of completely positive maps exactly when the Choi matrix of the sum is invertible or the fidelity vanishes: noisy channels of full Kraus rank are continuity points, unitary gates are not.
item.dc:creator: Morgan Jones

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. The two mean-square quantities are linearly comparable. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length, and the result extends to nonnegative observation weights with nonnegative Fourier transform. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Gap-Priced $|T\rangle$-States: Dynamic $|T\rangle$ Post-Selection and Budget-Aware Factory Provisioning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19299v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magic $|T\rangle$-state preparation dominates the cost of fault-tolerant quantum computation on surface codes, yet cultivation and distillation are typically provisioned statically, leaving much of the program's error budget unused. We present Gap-Priced $|T\rangle$ States (GP$|T\rangle$-S), a lattice surgery scheduler and factory allocator that co-optimizes both methods under a total $T$-error budget. GP$|T\rangle$-S uses the complementary gap of each cultivated state as a fidelity estimate and dynamically adjusts the cultivation gap cutoff, converting budget slack into speed by giving the scheduler control over the cultivation post-selection. GP$|T\rangle$-S also characterizes distillation factories by size, $|T\rangle$-state production rate, and budget slack, and introduces cultivating factories that embed cultivation within routing channels, achieving fidelities otherwise requiring two-level distillation at a single-level footprint. GP$|T\rangle$-S organizes these characterizations into a factory catalog, and performs distillation factory allocation over this catalog in tandem with the gap cutoff using dynamic-programming to achieve one of i) minimum spacetime volume, ii) minimum execution time, or iii) minimum space overhead, all within a user-provided $T$-error budget. Across sixteen benchmarks under high and low $T$-error budgets of $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-5}$ respectively, GP$|T\rangle$-S consistently outperforms cultivation-only and single-factory baselines without exceeding the budget, achieving a 5.5$\times$ geometric mean speedup in logical cycle count and a 3.4$\times$ geometric mean reduction in space-time volume.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Poster, Sayam Sethi, Steven Hofmeyr, Yuhao Liu, Jonathan Baker, Costin Iancu

item.title: A constructive solution to the $n$-representability problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.20737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an instantiation of the constructive solution to the fermionic quantum marginal problem by building the complete family of two-body witnesses at each level of a weighted sum-of-squares hierarchy. Our construction combines positive-semidefinite Gram matrices with explicit linear nullspace constraints that exactly cancel all higher-body contributions following a similar idea to the existing solution but made explicit in open source software. We demonstrate the weighted sum-of-squares construction numerically by solving the associated semidefinite program and recovering the exact ground-state energy of a Richardson Hamiltonian in the three-fermion sector. We further prove that higher-degree particle-number multipliers are unnecessary when the full sum-of-squares generating algebra is used.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas C. Rubin, A. Eugene DePrince III

item.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.23832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.
item.dc:creator: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Guang Hao Low, Ryan Babbush

item.title: Hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.28368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm for finding hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ over any effectively presented finite chain ring $R$. We call auxiliary group elements or subgroups used to extract information through oracle queries \emph{probes}. For chain length at least two, elementary abelian socle probes first recover the complete flag modulo the maximal ideal. When the residue field has size $q\ge3$, we reconstruct the flag recursively, lifting rank-one terminal members one digit at a time. The intermediate digits reduce to abelian hidden subgroup problems, while the final digit is a finite-field multiple-shift problem solved using learning from subset and Fourier sampling. For $q=2$, where distinct flags can have the same stabilizer, we instead lift the conjugate parabolic subgroup through the congruence filtration. A final linear system determines it modulo normalizer directions. The algorithm outputs generators with probability at least $1-\epsilon$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log|R|,\log(1/\epsilon))$. Consequences include $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})$ for every $N\ge2$ and, with an explicit maximal-order presentation, $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_K/N\mathcal{O}_K)$ for number fields $K$.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Imran

item.title: Comment on "InAs-Al hybrid devices passing the topological gap protocol", Microsoft Quantum, Phys. Rev. B 107, 245423 (2023)
item.description: arXiv:2502.19560v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological gap protocol (TGP) is presented as "a series of stringent experimental tests" for the presence of topological superconductivity and associated Majorana zero modes. Here, we show that the TGP, "passed" by Microsoft Quantum [PRB 107, 245423 (2023)], lacks a consistent definition of "gap" or "topological", and even utilises different code when applied to theoretical simulations compared to experimental data. Furthermore, the outcome of the TGP is sensitive to the choice of magnetic field range, bias voltage range, data resolution, and cutter voltage pair (junction transparency) -- data parameters that, in PRB 107, 245423 (2023), vary significantly, even for measurements of the same device. As a result, the core claims of PRB 107, 245423 (2023) are based on unexplained measurement choices and inconsistent definitions. In particular, this means the claim by Microsoft Quantum in PRB 107, 245423 (2023) that their devices have a "high probability of being in the topological phase" is not reliable and should be revisited. In light of this, subsequent studies that are based on tuning up devices via the TGP should also be revisited.
item.dc:creator: Henry F. Legg

item.title: Correlation of divergency: c_delta. Being different in a similar way or not
item.description: arXiv:2510.16717v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Matched sets may have unlike mean scores and spreads yet share the same way in which some scores stand apart. Mean gaps and raw-score correlations do not answer this question. Correlation of divergency, c_delta, is put forward to fill that gap. For every score in each of two equally sized, matched sets, it finds how far that score lies from every other score in its own set. It then draws these gaps into one divergence score through a power mean. The Pearson correlation between the two lists of divergence scores is c_delta, which lies between -1 and 1. A high positive value means that the same people or things stand out in both sets, no matter which way their raw scores point. A negative value means that a score far from the rest in one set tends to be matched with a score near the rest in the other, whilst a value near zero shows little linear link. As c_delta stems from within-set gaps, it is unchanged by shifts in overall level or units. It can show whether the same people feel sharply shut out in matched neighbourhood sets, whether the same bacterial strains grow oddly under two drugs, or whether the same proteins stand out in two drug-binding fingerprints. It should sit alongside means and raw-score correlations rather than take their place: c_delta does not show whether an outlier is high or low, nor why it arose. The power p sets the weight given to wide gaps. With p=1 it uses Gini distance, and with p=2 root-mean-square distance. Higher p gives more weight to the furthest gaps but cuts Kish's effective sample size. The raw scores and the choice of p must therefore be read with care.
item.dc:creator: Johan F. Hoorn, Johnny K. W. Ho

item.title: Electronic crystals and quasicrystals in semiconductor quantum wells: an AI-powered discovery
item.description: arXiv:2512.10909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The homogeneous electron gas is a cornerstone of quantum condensed matter physics, providing the foundation for developing density functional theory and understanding electronic phases in semiconductors. However, theoretical understanding of strongly-correlated electrons in realistic semiconductor systems remains limited. In this work, we develop a neural network based variational approach to study quantum wells in three dimensional geometry for a variety of electron densities and well thicknesses. Starting from first principles, our unbiased AI-powered method reveals metallic and crystalline phases with both monolayer and bilayer charge distributions. In the emergent bilayer, we discover a new quantum phase of matter: the electronic quasicrystal.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Gaggioli, Pierre-Antoine Graham, Liang Fu

item.title: Graph-Theoretic Formulation of Hamiltonian and Ground-State Sign Structures in Heisenberg Antiferromagnets
item.description: arXiv:2602.04943v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Heisenberg antiferromagnets through a graph-theoretic representation of their Hamiltonians. In the computational basis of a fixed-magnetization sector, the Heisenberg Hamiltonian equals a constant minus the weighted Laplacian of a graph whose vertices are spin configurations and whose edges connect configurations related by exchanging two antiparallel spins on a lattice bond. We call this graph the Hilbert graph (HG) which is isomorphic to the token graph of the lattice over which the Hamiltonian is defined. The exact ground-state energy is then determined by the largest eigenvalue of the HG Laplacian, which is the spectral relaxation of weighted Max-Cut on the HG. With the amplitudes fixed, the phase-dependent part of the variational energy defines an antiferromagnetic classical XY model on the HG, with couplings set by the amplitudes. Restricting the variational state to be real, i.e., restricting its phases to $\{0,\pi\}$, reduces the fixed-amplitude energy minimization to solving an antiferromagnetic Ising model and hence a weighted Max-Cut on the HG. When the weights are generated from non-degenerate ground-state amplitudes, the optimal phases give the ground-state sign structure which can be recovered from the weights in time polynomial in the size of the HG. On the Hamiltonian side, a diagonal sign transformation removes all positive off-diagonal matrix elements if and only if the HG is bipartite, which reproduces the Marshall sign rule on bipartite lattices through the graph two-coloring problem; otherwise, the minimal remaining positive weight equals the sum of HG edge weights left uncut by the Max-Cut. This graph formulation establishes a common framework for understanding wave function sign structure, Hamiltonian stoquasticity, non-convexity of phase optimization in variational Monte Carlo, and the average sign in quantum Monte Carlo.
item.dc:creator: Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Nobuchika Okada, Paulo T. Araujo

item.title: Edge universality in Floquet sideband spectra
item.description: arXiv:2604.05244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A monochromatic voltage drive redistributes noninteracting fermions over sidebands with Bessel amplitudes. A sharp Fermi step gives the discrete Bessel source kernel, whose large amplitude edge has the Airy limit known from random matrices and propagating fronts. At zero temperature and for energy independent transmission, the deficit of the dc bias derivative of low frequency partition noise from its large bias slope is proportional to the kernel diagonal, with ac amplitude fixed. Shifting the integer threshold coordinate down by half a sideband removes the leading finite amplitude correction. For reservoirs at a common temperature, we derive the rescaled deficit's crossover through one thermal convolution per reservoir. Its leading low temperature correction is twice that of the rescaled source occupation. We specify the geometry and mode resolution needed to distinguish this signature from the full Airy point process.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: Mixed-State Topology in One-Dimensional Open Floquet Systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.25248v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the non-equilibrium topology of the steady state of a periodically driven, dissipative Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain using the ensemble geometric phase (EGP) $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}$, a generalisation of the Zak phase to mixed states. The coupling to thermal reservoirs is treated microscopically within Floquet-Born-Markov theory without the rotating-wave approximation. We classify the steady state rather than the generator of the dynamics, using its purity spectrum as the analogue of a band structure. We show that, within the EGP framework, the $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ structure of isolated chiral-symmetric Floquet SSH systems generally does not carry over to the steady state. Instead, the steady state carries a single invariant whose type is set by an underlying symmetry. When this symmetry holds, the invariant is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-valued, with quantised $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}=\pm\pi/2$ at all times and finite temperatures. The EGP can switch within a driving period, tracking the presence of edge modes in the open-boundary purity spectrum and thereby establishing a bulk-boundary correspondence. The fraction of each period spent in the nontrivial regime varies continuously with the driving frequency, and the switching disappears if the dependence of the dissipator on the drive is neglected. When the symmetry is broken, $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}$ is no longer quantised, but its winding over a drive period $T$ defines an invariant $\nu_T \in \mathbb Z$, with no purity-spectrum bulk-boundary correspondence. We propose that its changes signal temperature- and frequency-driven topological phase transitions. Our formalism extends to general quadratic fermionic systems with linear bath couplings.
item.dc:creator: G\"orkem D. Dinc, Alexander Schnell, Andy M. Martin

item.title: Adaptive Entangled Neurons in the Brain and Natural Intelligence Simulations for Artificial General Intelligence
item.description: arXiv:2609.09226v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding the brain's mechanisms is crucial in neuroscience, particularly for simulating natural intelligence and advancing artificial general intelligence (AGI). Liu et al. (2024) and Deco et al. (2025) propose that quantum entanglement may underlie the synchronization of millions of neurons, introducing the Liu-Chen-Ao (LCA) hypothesis of entangled nerve fibers. However, directly testing this idea remains challenging. Here we employ a nonlocal many-body wave equation, introducing a generalized probability-wave framework to model collective behaviors among adaptive, interacting agents, particles, or neurons. This approach enables testable eigenmodes, offering an indirect means of examining the LCA hypothesis by observing patterns in collective trading behaviors. These patterns, rooted in behavioral psychology, are thought to mirror the internal brain's decision-making and underlying mechanisms. Our analysis of Chinese intraday stock market data shows that adaptive entangled game modes explain 82%-94% of decision patterns, sharply contrasting neoclassical finance predictions assuming independent rational agents. Additionally, 2-12% of actions adapt to news, events, and environmental changes, marked by rapid equilibrium shifts, while truly independent behaviors make up less than 5%. These results empirically support the LCA hypothesis and underscore the need to simulate the brain's mechanisms and generate adaptive, entangled modules for AGI. They also expose the shortcomings of conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) that depend on vast, opaque parameters. By combining ANN-based AI with probability-wave-based entangled brain simulations, machine learning enables the creation of human-like processing units (HPUs). Such HPUs promise more efficient and robust AGI, particularly for embodied intelligence and robotics.
item.dc:creator: Haochen Li, Xinshuai Guo, Jingdong Ouyang, Wei Zhang, Leilei Shi

item.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert-Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Li

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is the third of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on simple unstable theories. The Pauli group of quantum error correction, with anticommutation as its relation, has a simple unstable theory, like the random graph. Forking and the Kim--Pillay independence theorem acquire a meaning in stabilizer codes: forking recognizes logical errors, and the independence theorem glues syndromes.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~{n}ez, Jos\'{e} Iovino

item.title: A group theoretic calculation of multi-invariants of some stabilizer states
item.description: arXiv:2610.27098v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study multi-invariants---a multi-partite generalization of Renyi entropies---of simple stabilizer states, for an arbitrary replica symmetry group. We develop a group theoretic technique for evaluating such invariants, which operates on the replica group and involves counting intersections among its cosets. Our techniques streamline the calculations of multi-invariants for graph states with two GHZ-like nodes and for certain generalizations thereof. The methodology developed here is most suitable when the quantum state is simple but flexibility over the replica group is desired.
item.dc:creator: Bartlomiej Czech, Yichen Feng, Jonathan Harper, Xin-Xiang Ju
